- changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md:21 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5

- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:1240-1247 (cached_file_missing skip block in collect) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The cached_file_missing skip handling checks run.get("reused") and records missing files and artifacts under "cached_file_missing", but reused is never True in production after the Actions cache steps were removed.
  WHY: The code does not fail at runtime; it is unreachable dead code, and the tests exercise a scenario where the same stage calls collect twice for the same issue, which the workflow never does.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:render_index lines 1350-1351 (the "(missing from cache)" label) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The ternary expression produces " (missing from cache)" as the file label for jobs whose entry matches a cached_file_missing skip.
  WHY: Since reused=True is never set in production, the cached_file_missing skip reason is never recorded, so this label is never rendered.

  Expected change site: The action/cache steps removed from clarify.yml, plan.yml, and implement.yml

README.md lines 1424-1428 now read "20 REST calls per stage, since each stage collects its own evidence. The evidence is not cached between stages because Actions caches are readable by pull-request runs." The core deliverable is implemented.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5 (gap is closed - implementation is present)

  Expected change site: agents.md line 213
  Evidence of absence: The requirement is satisfied. agents.md line 213 now reads "400 KB, fetched separately by each stage without an Actions cache, which pull-request runs can read)." The old wording was replaced in the original PR diff.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5 (gap is closed - implementation is present)

  WHY: When scripts/assemble_changelog.py runs at release time, this unrelated merge-guard documentation will be folded into CHANGELOG.md under the #6055 entry, corrupting release notes and misattributing changes across unrelated issues.
- changelog.d/6247-heal-evidence-no-cache.md:1-4 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The changelog fragment omits the audience closing paragraph ("What this means for <audience>:") and the lead paragraph has only two sentences instead of the required three to five sentences.
  WHY: The fragment violates the mandatory changelog structure contract in CLAUDE.md section 20.D, which requires a 3-5 sentence lead paragraph and an explicit operational takeaway paragraph for the audience.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:1415
  PROBLEM: purge_legacy_evidence_caches relies on the CLI parser in main() for repository slug validation; programmatic callers passing an unchecked repo argument could issue malformed API requests.
  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: Add a defensive guard `if not heal.is_valid_repo_slug(repo): return {**result, "status": "invalid_repo"}` at the start of purge_legacy_evidence_caches.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:lines 1240-1247 (the new `for run in runs` block before `_enforce_total_budget`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `cached_file_missing` skip branch and the artifact twin only fire when `run.get("reused")` is truthy, but each trusted stage now starts with a fresh `${RUNNER_TEMP}/heal-evidence` after the Actions cache steps were removed.
  WHY: The branch, skip-reason values, and test cover a code path the production workflow no longer performs; the defensive code does not break anything but is dead and misleading.
- Requirement: Workflow-heal evidence must not live in a PR-readable Actions cache (issue #6247 / linked security finding). The remediation fragments added by the PR must be released under their own issues, not contaminate unrelated fragments.
  Expected change site: changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md
  Evidence of absence: Line 21 of `changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md` ends with a paragraph that begins "The consumer merge guard template distinguishes a numeric file-descriptor prefix (`2>/dev/null`) from a separated or quoted numeric push refspec (`2 > /dev/null`), checking the branch actually pushed in either case…" This paragraph belongs to PR #6133's `changelog.d/6133-pr-merge-guard-live-copy-sync.md` (line 4 of that fragment is the canonical source for the same wording). It was introduced into the #6055 fragment by the `[ai-merge-resolve]` commit (8e85534 in `last_commit_stat.txt`) and will be folded into the published #6055 changelog entry by `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` at release time, mis-attributing consumer-merge-guard work to a heal-evidence release note.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: Each PR that changes observable behaviour ships one changelog fragment conforming to the structure in CLAUDE.md §20.D.4 — headline, lead paragraph (3-5 sentences), "The numbers that matter" table when measurable details exist, "What this means for <audience>:" closing, optional "For contributors" subsection.
  Expected change site: changelog.d/6247-heal-evidence-no-cache.md
  Evidence of absence: The fragment has only four lines. The lead is two sentences (line 2 and the single sentence on line 4), short of the 3-5 sentence floor. There is no "The numbers that matter" table (the per-stage ~20-call count, the 7-day cache eviction, the one-list-plus-one-delete API shape, the fork-PR read vector, and the eligible-heal-issue scope are all measurable details that belong in a table). There is no "What this means for operators:" or analogous audience closing, and no "For contributors" subsection.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
